name: Question 6
worked_solution:
First, we compute ${A}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${A}^{2}=A,$ so $A$ is an idempotent matrix. 

We can use this fact to compute ${A}^{4}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{4} & ={A}^{2}\cdot {A}^{2} \\  & =A\cdot A \\  & ={A}^{2} \\  & =A\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{A}^{4}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

A2=A⋅A=[1000220−1−1]⋅[1000220−1−1]=[1000220−1−1]=A

Notice that A2=A, so A is an idempotent matrix.

A4=A2⋅A2=A⋅A=A2=A

A4=[1000220−1−1].
